Slats shifting backward and upward causes them to rest elevated on top of the stationary blocks.

caption: An overhead view shows a pale pine panel lying flat on a white tabletop. A pair of hands carries two small rectangular wooden blocks in from below and sets them on the panel, one on the left third and one on the right third, before releasing and withdrawing. The two blocks then rest at fixed positions on the bare surface. A long flat slat appears lying across the front edge of the panel. It is then shifted backward and upward until it rests on top of the blocks, elevated above the surface, while two hands grip its ends to hold and fine-tune this position before withdrawing. A second, rounded-edge slat is then brought in from below and laid flat on the panel in front of the blocks. The hands keep holding its two ends and adjust it through the final frames. Throughout, the panel and the two blocks stay put as the slats and hands move relative to them.
